newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Council meets on Turkey, Yugoslavia.
newsitem.headline: Council meets on Turkey, Yugoslavia.

text.p: The General Affairs Council met on Monday for a low-key meeting on issues including policy toward the former Yugoslavia and relations with southeastern neighbour Turkey.
Ministers were also to discuss the situation in Africa's Great Lakes region, East Timor, and the Middle East.
In one of the only decisions expected from the meeting, ministers were expected to extend for a further six months sanctions on Nigeria imposed because of the alleged human rights violations.
"The general human rights situation and the pace and the manner of the transition to civil democratic rule (in Nigeria) continue to give rise to concern," ministers said in a draft statement.
On Yugoslavia, the ministers were to hear from international high representative Carl Bildt on the latest situation in Bosnia.
In Serbia on Sunday, authorities annulled an opposition election victory in Belgrade, leading to charges that President Slobodan Milosevic was making a mockery of the democratic process.

The Irish EU presidency plans to launch a discussion over lunch about the bloc's relations with Turkey. Although a customs agreement with Ankara is in force, funds to help Turkey to develop have been blocked.
EU member Greece maintains a hard stance against Turkey, which it accuses of having designs on Greek territory.
